html:
The Tenino are a Sahaptin-speaking people of north-central Oregon, along the Deschutes River and the Columbia River. The map spells their name Tenimo.

They lived near Celilo Falls, one of the richest salmon fisheries and trading places in North America, where peoples from the coast, the plateau and the plains met. Their neighbours were the Chinookan Wasco on the river and the Yakama to the north.

Under an 1855 treaty the Tenino and related bands moved to the Warm Springs Reservation, and they form part of the Confederated Tribes of Warm Springs today. The map also shows them as Tenino.
